newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Thieves and rapists in S.African government guard.
newsitem.headline: Thieves and rapists in S.African government guard.

text.p: More than a tenth of those in South Africa's National Protection Service, which looks after President Nelson Mandela and his government, are facing criminal charges.
Minister of Safety and Security Sydney Mufamadi said in a written response to a parliamentary question that 120 of the 1,800 service members had criminal records.
A further 198 currently faced charges ranging from murder to kidnapping, assault, theft and drunken driving.
Mufamadi tabled a list showing that convictions included five of attempted murder, two of rape, eight of assault, 10 of theft, 13 of drunken driving, two of kidnapping and two of armed robbery.

Charges pending against members of the unit include 22 of murder, nine of housebreaking, four of armed robbery, 18 of attempted murder, 21 of theft, 23 of assault, four of rape and one of public indecency.
The problem of those supposed to protect South Africa's government surfaced when ministers and President Nelson Mandela were found to have suffered a rash of thefts from their homes.
